effective_source: ISO 32000-2:2020 with Errata Collection 3; checked in doc/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf and searchable doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md. The source-layout split plus ISO footer locates §9.7.3 at physical p. 344 / printed p. 329, §9.7.6.1 at physical pp. 355-356 / printed pp. 340-341, and §9.9.1/Table 124-125 at physical pp. 366-368 / printed pp. 351-353.
overall: The inspected CID/CMap mapping and OpenType selection paths align with the source features reviewed. The strongest discovered test opportunity is a deterministic PDF integration assertion for Type 2 big-endian CIDToGIDMap and short-map CID-0 fallback. No current behavior failure is established. This review does not certify all of §9.7 or all OpenType file conformance.

features.source: md:8008-8023. Registry+Ordering identify a collection; Supplement is required but must not determine compatibility; compatibility is Registry and Ordering. Errata #518 removes arrays of CIDSystemInfo dictionaries from CMaps; doc/errata-read.md:109 records the implementation as unaffected.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/composite.rs:379-415 reads descendant Registry/Ordering; predefined collection lookup is in composite.rs and predefined.rs.
assertions: composite.rs unit tests cover absent/malformed collection names and carried collection cases; CMap tests exercise Adobe collection names
features.assessment: The role of Supplement is not used as a compatibility key, consistent with source. The erratum concerns producer structure; do not infer a reader rejection requirement from it. Detailed conformance of every CMap/descendant pair is outside this shard.

features.source: md:8030-8095. Type0 CIDFont routes use CFF charset for CID-keyed CFF, CIDs as GIDs for name-keyed CFF, or Type 2 CIDToGIDMap. Table 115 says stream entry byte 2*c is high-order byte. §9.7.6.3 requires CID-0 fallback when the map has no corresponding GID.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/composite.rs:18-66 and 260-375; crates/pdf-font/src/loading/glyphs.rs:248-254 applies CMap CID, notdef CID, then CID 0.
assertions: pdf-model/tests/composite_fonts.rs::the_cid_widths_agree_with_the_font_programs_own_advances (independent /W vs manually-read hmtx, but optional corpus inputs)
pdf-model/tests/ocr_text_layer.rs uses a deterministic remapping stream but its glyph programs are intentionally hollow
pdf-transform/src/archive/font_files.rs tests cover stream mappings in conversion, not the ordinary reader
features.assessment: Implementation visibly follows byte-order and fallback clauses. Existing reader test evidence is either corpus-dependent or uses hollow glyphs; draft in drafts/cid_map_big_endian_and_short_fallback.rs supplies fixed known GIDs, a positive mapped code, a short-map fallback code, an exact xref assertion, and the public page interpretation.

features.source: md:8070-8125. W supports consecutive-CID arrays and CID ranges; duplicated CID specifications use first specification. DW defaults 1000. DW2 defaults [880 -1000]; horizontal position component is half width and horizontal displacement zero. W2 uses three-number metric tuples; writing mode is determined by CMap.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/metrics.rs:480-610 parses W; Vertical::read around 768-825 reads DW2/W2; advances/position in loading/advances.rs.
assertions: DW2 source example and alternative control tests in same fixture module
pdf-model/tests/composite_fonts.rs tests vertical.pdf and corpus stream map against hmtx
features.assessment: Strong source-derived numeric controls for array/range/default and duplicate-W behavior. The tests assert answers at metric API, rather than only parser acceptance. Producer rule that W2 is only for vertical writing is not treated as a reader rejection rule.

features.feature: CMap mapping, codespaces, predefined maps, UseCMap and stream declarations
features.source: md:8129-8290. CMap maps variable-length codes to CIDs and supplies writing mode; codespaces have length <=4 and non-overlapping ranges; mapping lookup is by code length; named predefined CMaps or streams are supported. /UseCMap inheritance and file usecmap must agree. EC3 #278 only strikes stray punctuation in §9.7.5.3; errata table at doc/errata-read.md:2716.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/cmap.rs; composite.rs:70-243 reads names/streams, inherited maps, WMode and code space; predefined CMaps in data/cmaps.
assertions: crates/pdf-font/src/cmap.rs unit tests for bytewise ranges, first mappings, notdef ranges and usecmap
composite_fonts.rs::a_bfchar_in_an_encoding_cmap_selects_a_cid is a malformed-producer recovery policy, not a valid-file requirement
features.assessment: Core codespace and mapping behavior has discriminating synthetic controls; CMap clipping is bounded and reported. EC3 #518's CMap CIDSystemInfo array change was checked separately. Do not state rejection of nonconforming CMap syntax as a normative reader obligation.

features.feature: Type 0 root dictionary, decoding and undefined-code fallbacks
features.source: md:8295-8340. Root has a single descendant CIDFont; codespace determines byte count; mapping results use font index 0 and CID; missing requested CID tries notdef mappings, then CID 0; invalid codes consume length based on the best partial codespace match; short CIDToGIDMap falls back to GID for CID 0.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/loading.rs:964-1005 loads Type 0 descendant; cmap.rs Code tracks value, length and codespace membership; loading/glyphs.rs:248-254 implements final fallback order.
assertions: cmap.rs unit test for notdef ranges kept apart from character mappings
no one inspected fixture was found asserting all notdef->CID0 fallback stages through the public page reader
features.assessment: Mapping logic and source-order behavior are explicit. Malformed root dictionary cardinalities are reader policy; valid Table 119 one-descendant inputs are the scope here. Draft isolates the map stream branch of the public fallback. A full invalid-code partial-match PDF fixture remains residual.

features.feature: Embedded OpenType format and glyph selection by wrapped table/font dictionary
features.source: md:8500-8570. Table 124 splits OpenType with glyf for TrueType/CIDFontType2, CFF with CID operators for CIDFontType0, and name-keyed CFF for Type1 or CIDFontType0. §9.9.1 Type1+CFF uses §9.6.5.2 name selection; TrueType+glyf follows §9.6.5.4. OpenType program conformance refers to ISO/IEC 14496-22:2019. Table 125 Length1-3 rules are for Type1/TrueType, not CFF.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/loading/opening.rs:95-111 and 421-446 selects named CFF in Type1/MMType1 wrapper; composite.rs:260-328 handles CFF inside CID fonts; program.rs:131 onward selects OpenType program tables.
features.assessment: These exact-xref tests assert nonempty selected GIDs with swapped-glyph positive controls, not just successful font loading. They cover all four Type 1/TrueType + CFF/glyf selection cases relevant to ADR 2817. They do not assert complete ISO/IEC 14496-22 validation or every table-presence requirement.

features.source: EC3 Table 109 (outside §9.9), Standard 14 widths may be omitted; Table 109 /Widths required otherwise. This baseline changes the published metric read when Widths absent.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/loading/opening.rs::published_metrics changed wording/decision; crates/pdf-font/src/metrics.rs adds unit test a_substitute_with_no_widths_keeps_the_resembling_standard_metrics and standard-14 positive control.
assertions: metrics.rs tests assert Helvetica A advance 667/1000 for no-width substitute with or without descriptor, and standard14 control despite MissingWidth 300
features.assessment: The numeric expectation is from the standard face's published metrics and has a control. Policy question Q859 remains explicitly unresolved for non-Standard14 substitute/descriptor MissingWidth semantics; don't broaden this as an unconditional §9.9 duty.

not_claimed: All PDF-reader behavior for malformed CMaps or Type 0 dictionaries
